title: 2020 AMC 10A Problem 22
statement: For how many positive integers \(n \le 1000\) is\[\left\lfloor \dfrac{998}{n} \right\rfloor+\left\lfloor \dfrac{999}{n} \right\rfloor+\left\lfloor \dfrac{1000}{n}\right \rfloor\]not divisible by \(3?\) (Recall that \(\lfloor x \rfloor\) is the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x.\))

solutions.text:
Write \(1000=qn+r\), where \(0\le r<n\). Then \(\left\lfloor\dfrac{1000}{n}\right\rfloor=q\). The other two floors are usually also \(q\), except that subtracting \(1\) or \(2\) from \(1000\) crosses a multiple of \(n\) when \(r\) is small.

For \(n>1\), the sum is not divisible by \(3\) exactly when \(r=0\) or \(r=1\). The case \(r=0\) gives divisors of \(1000\), excluding \(1\), for \(15\) values. The case \(r=1\) gives divisors of \(999\), excluding \(1\), for \((3+1)(1+1)-1=7\) values. The total is \(22\). Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: The sum of floors fails to be a multiple of \(3\) only when subtracting \(1\) or \(2\) crosses a multiple of \(n\)
